# Base Documentation

> ## Agent Instructions
> For the current source of truth, read https://docs.base.org/llms.txt and connect the Base docs MCP server at https://docs.base.org/mcp.

- [Base](https://docs.base.org/index.md): Start building on Base, the blockchain for global finance: connect your agent or tools, choose a solution, find network details and funds, and track network upgrades.
- [Base](https://docs.base.org/get-started/base.md): The blockchain for global finance.
- [Connect to Base](https://docs.base.org/get-started/connect-to-base.md): Network details for Base Mainnet and Base Sepolia: RPC endpoints, chain IDs, and block explorers.
- [Get Funds](https://docs.base.org/get-started/get-funds.md): Fund an address on Base: withdraw from a Coinbase account, bridge from another chain, or use a testnet faucet.
- [Make a Transaction](https://docs.base.org/get-started/make-a-transaction.md): Send your first transaction on Base with viem: connect, sign, and confirm in seconds for a fraction of a cent.
- [Bridge to Base](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/network-information/ecosystem-bridges.md): Move ETH, stablecoins, and tokens to and from Base using the standard bridge, fast bridges, aggregators, or cross-chain messaging protocols.
- [Integrate DeFi](https://docs.base.org/get-started/integrate-defi.md): Add trading with the 0x Swap API, or lending, collateralized borrowing, and a vault-based earn product with the Base Earn API on Base.
- [Tokenize Assets](https://docs.base.org/get-started/issue-rwa.md): Represent and operate real-world assets on Base with the B20 Asset standard: configurable precision, issuer roles, holder controls, and distributions through one ERC-20-compatible surface.
- [Issue a Stablecoin](https://docs.base.org/get-started/issue-stablecoins.md): Run a fiat-backed stablecoin on Base with minting, compliance, and reconciliation built into the chain.
- [Accept Payments](https://docs.base.org/get-started/accept-payments.md): Choose an onchain payment lifecycle for commerce checkout, agentic payments, reconciliation, refunds, and payouts on Base.
- [Private Transactions](https://docs.base.org/get-started/private-transactions.md): Run confidential enterprise payments on Base with Base Ledgers: balances, transfers, and counterparties stay private while funds settle onchain.
- [Resources for AI Agents](https://docs.base.org/get-started/resources-for-ai-agents.md): Base-first resources for AI agents, including docs indexes, MCP access, skills, and recommended starting points
- [MCP Server](https://docs.base.org/get-started/docs-mcp.md): Connect your AI coding assistant to Base documentation using Model Context Protocol for real-time access.
- [Static Docs Files](https://docs.base.org/get-started/docs-llms.md): Use llms.txt and llms-full.txt to give AI assistants access to Base documentation.
- [Base Batches](https://docs.base.org/get-started/base-batches.md): Apply to Base Batches, an accelerator with investment, mentorship, and a demo day for early-stage teams building on Base.
- [Base Ecosystem Fund](https://docs.base.org/get-started/base-ecosystem-fund.md): The Base Ecosystem Fund backs pre-seed and seed teams building onchain businesses on Base, in partnership with Coinbase Ventures.
- [Builder Stack](https://docs.base.org/get-started/builder-stack.md): A collection of credits & discounts on software for building on Base
- [Builders](https://docs.base.org/get-started/builders.md): Find the support Base offers at every stage of building onchain, from tutorials and communities to grants and accelerators.
- [Creators](https://docs.base.org/get-started/creators.md): Grant support from Base for independent creators making content about Base.
- [Base Protocol](https://docs.base.org/get-started/base-chain.md): Explore Base as a chain: connect to its networks, use native primitives, understand transactions and network systems, and operate infrastructure.
- [SDKs & APIs](https://docs.base.org/get-started/sdks-and-apis.md): Choose the Base SDK, API, or CLI that matches what you are building.
- [Build on Base](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/overview.md): Build financial products on Base by outcome: integrate DeFi, tokenize assets, issue stablecoins, accept payments, or run private transactions.
- [Test on Vibenet](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/test-on-vibenet.md): Build and test against Base's newest chain-level features on Vibenet, Base's experimental preview network, and track what's live at chain.base.org/vibenet.
- [Run a Local Devnet](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/run-a-local-devnet.md): Run Base locally from the base/base repo: a fresh Docker devnet with L1, sequencer, and batcher, or a snapshot devnet that continues Base Mainnet state and lets you act as any account.
- [Deploy a Smart Contract](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/deploy-a-smart-contract.md): How smart contracts work on Base, which Foundry versions support Base's native precompiles and the Denim upgrade, and how to deploy a contract to Base Sepolia with Foundry.
- [Assign User Attributes](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/assign-user-attributes.md): Choose Builder Codes for transaction attribution or Base Verify for verified user traits, identity deduplication, and eligibility policies.
- [Integrate an Earn Product](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/integrate-earn-product.md): Build a one-deposit earn experience on Base with the Base Earn API: a vault catalog, live positions, and redeemable value.
- [Integrate Lending](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/integrate-lending.md): Let users deposit into Morpho and Upshift vaults on Base and withdraw again through the Base Earn API.
- [Integrate Borrowing](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/integrate-borrowing.md): Let users borrow from Morpho Blue markets on Base against supported collateral through the Base Earn API.
- [Integrate Trading](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/integrate-trading.md): Let users swap tokens on Base with executable routes from the 0x Swap API.
- [List Tokenized Stocks](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/integrate-defi/list-tokenized-stocks.md): Let users trade Coinbase-issued tokenized stocks on your app.
- [Create an Asset Token](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-rwa/create-an-asset-token.md): Create a six-decimal B20 Asset token with issuer roles, a supply ceiling, and issuer-defined metadata. This example configures a stock token.
- [Issue Units to Holders](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-rwa/issue-units.md): Distribute B20 Asset units to multiple approved holders in one batch.
- [Restrict Eligible Holders](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-rwa/restrict-eligible-holders.md): Keep units within an approved set of holders by binding a B20 allowlist to issuance and transfers.
- [Restrict Who Can Initiate Transfers](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-rwa/restrict-transfer-initiators.md): Control which account may initiate a B20 transfer, separately from who may send or receive, by binding an allowlist to TRANSFER_EXECUTOR_POLICY. Routing every transfer through a transfer agent is one example.
- [Seize and Cancel Units](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-rwa/seize-and-cancel-units.md): Move units from a holder who is no longer eligible into a safekeeping account with B20 seizeWithMemo, then cancel them with a memo'd burn.
- [Announce a Change to Holders](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-rwa/announce-a-distribution.md): Wrap a holder-impacting change on a B20 Asset with an onchain disclosure using announce: additional issuance, multiplier updates, treasury burns, or a notice with no onchain effect.
- [Apply a Multiplier](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-rwa/apply-a-multiplier.md): Schedule a B20 Asset multiplier update so displayed unit counts change at a future time without rewriting raw balances. A stock split is one example.
- [Pause Transfers](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-rwa/pause-transfers.md): Pause transfers on a B20 Asset token during an incident while leaving minting and burning available.
- [Issue Your Stablecoin](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-stablecoins/issue-your-stablecoin.md): Create a fiat-backed stablecoin on Base with one B20 factory call.
- [Mint Supply](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-stablecoins/mint-supply.md): Issue new stablecoin supply on Base as reserves grow, gated by a minter role and an optional supply cap.
- [Burn Supply](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-stablecoins/burn-supply.md): Retire stablecoin supply on Base when a holder redeems for fiat, keeping circulating supply matched to reserves.
- [Restrict Who Can Hold It](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-stablecoins/restrict-who-can-hold.md): Limit transfers of your stablecoin to accounts your KYC program has approved, using B20 transfer policies.
- [Block an Account](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-stablecoins/block-an-account.md): Stop a specific address from moving your stablecoin when a compliance hold requires it, without affecting other holders.
- [Recover Funds](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-stablecoins/recover-funds.md): Move a stablecoin balance out of a blocked account into a safekeeping account on Base, for lost keys or a legal hold, without changing total supply.
- [Pause Activity](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-stablecoins/pause-activity.md): Halt transfers, mints, or burns on your stablecoin independently during an incident, then resume when it's resolved.
- [Reconcile with Memos](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/issue-stablecoins/reconcile-with-memos.md): Tag stablecoin operations with an onchain reference so you can match them to offchain records at scale.
- [Make a Simple Payment](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/make-a-simple-payment.md): Send USDC directly from one wallet to another on Base.
- [Request a Payment](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/request-a-payment.md): Request and settle an immediate escrow-backed charge on Base.
- [Authorize a Payment](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/authorize-a-payment.md): Move payer funds into escrow for later capture on Base.
- [Capture an Authorization](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/capture-an-authorization.md): Capture all or part of an escrowed authorization, in one capture or across multiple fulfillment increments, before the authorization expires.
- [Charge on a Schedule](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/charge-on-a-schedule.md): Create one escrow-backed charge per billing period using a wallet spend permission.
- [Verify a Payment](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/verify-a-payment.md): Verify confirmed escrow events and claim each settlement exactly once before fulfillment.
- [Watch for Payments](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/watch-for-payments.md): Watch escrow events, backfill missed blocks, and process confirmed lifecycle changes idempotently.
- [Reconcile Payments](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/reconcile-payments.md): Build a settlement report from escrow charges, captures, fees, voids, reclaims, and refunds.
- [Refund a Payment](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/refund-a-payment.md): Return captured value to the original payer within the refund window.
- [Void an Authorization](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/void-an-authorization.md): Return the remaining escrowed authorization to the payer or let the payer reclaim it after expiry.
- [Send a Payout](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/send-a-payout.md): Send a referenced batch of token payouts in one transaction without leaving funds in the payout contract.
- [Split a Payment](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/split-a-payment.md): Split one token amount across marketplace recipients with exact basis-point accounting and no stranded dust.
- [Charge for an API](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/charge-for-an-api.md): Protect a fixed-price API route with the x402 exact scheme on Base.
- [Settle Usage-Based Payments](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/settle-usage-based-payments.md): Authorize a maximum x402 payment and settle the actual API usage after the handler succeeds.
- [Batch High-Frequency Payments](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/batch-high-frequency-payments.md): Verify cumulative x402 vouchers per request and settle high-frequency API usage in batches.
- [Call a Paid Service](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/accept-payments/call-a-paid-service.md): Call an x402 service from an agent while enforcing network, token, per-request, and session spend limits.
- [Deposit to a Ledger](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/ledgers/deposit.md): Move funds from Base into a private ledger through the Portal contract, with the recipient encrypted onchain.
- [Transfer Inside a Ledger](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/ledgers/transfer.md): Move balances between accounts inside a ledger while keeping the sender, recipient, and amount off the public chain.
- [Withdraw From a Ledger](https://docs.base.org/build-on-base/ledgers/withdraw.md): Move funds from a ledger back to Base through the Portal contract, keeping the account behind the withdrawal private.
- [Base Specifications](https://docs.base.org/specifications/overview.md): Base protocol specifications — tokens, bridging, transactions, consensus, execution, and proofs.
- [Base Protocol Overview](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/overview.md): High-level overview of the Base Chain protocol — network participants, system architecture, core components, and user flows.
- [Specification](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/consensus/specification.md): Specification of the Base rollup node, describing its components and role in L2 block derivation and consensus.
- [Derivation](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/consensus/derivation.md): Specification of the L2 chain derivation pipeline, describing how L2 blocks are deterministically derived from L1 data and sequencer batches.
- [P2P](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/consensus/p2p.md): Specification of the rollup node peer-to-peer network, covering node discovery, gossip protocol, and unsafe block propagation.
- [RPC](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/consensus/rpc.md): Specification of the rollup node RPC interface, including the optimism_outputAtBlock method for retrieving L2 output roots.
- [L2 Execution Engine](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/execution/l2-execution-engine.md): Specification of the L2 execution engine, detailing EIP-1559 parameters, fee vaults, Engine API usage, and execution layer behavior.
- [Precompiles](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/execution/precompiles.md): Specification of precompiled contracts on Base, including native EVM implementations available at predefined addresses.
- [Predeploys](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/execution/predeploys.md): Specification of predeployed smart contracts on Base, including system contracts deployed at predetermined addresses in genesis state.
- [Preinstalls](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/execution/preinstalls.md): Specification of preinstalled smart contracts on Base, including utility contracts deployed in genesis state that run directly in the EVM.
- [Standard Bridges](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/bridging/standard-bridges.md): Specification of the standard bridge contracts enabling cross-domain ETH and ERC-20 token transfers between L1 and L2 on Base.
- [Deposits](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/bridging/deposits.md): How deposits work on Base — from user experience to the protocol-level deposit transaction type and guaranteed gas market.
- [Withdrawals](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/bridging/withdrawals.md): How withdrawals work on Base — the standard 3-step flow, the finalization window (5 days, or 1 day with TEE and ZK proofs), faster options, and the full protocol specification.
- [Cross Domain Messengers](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/bridging/cross-domain-messengers.md): Specification of the cross-domain messenger contracts, providing a higher-level API for sending messages between L1 and L2 on Base.
- [Base-Solana Bridge](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/bridging/base-solana-bridge.md): Bridge tokens and messages between Base and Solana Mainnet
- [Batcher](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/batcher.md): Specification of the batcher (batch submitter), the component responsible for posting L2 sequencer data to L1 for data availability.
- [Base Proofs](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/proofs/overview.md): Overview of the offchain services and onchain contracts that make L2 checkpoint proposals verifiable from Ethereum in the Azul proof system.
- [Challenger](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/proofs/challenger.md): Specification of the challenger, an offchain service that detects invalid AggregateVerifier games and submits dispute transactions on L1 to nullify them.
- [Proposer](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/proofs/proposer.md): Specification of the proposer, an offchain service that turns canonical L2 checkpoint ranges into AggregateVerifier games on L1.
- [Registrar](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/proofs/registrar.md): Specification of the registrar and the hinted P-384 flow used to register AWS Nitro Enclave signer identities on L1.
- [TEE Prover](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/proofs/tee-prover.md): Specification of the TEE prover, an offchain service that re-executes L2 block ranges inside AWS Nitro Enclaves to produce signed proof material for AggregateVerifier games.
- [ZK Prover](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/proofs/zk-prover.md): Specification of the ZK prover, an offchain service that uses SP1 programs to produce permissionless proofs for checkpoint proposals and disputes.
- [Proof Contracts](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/proofs/proof-contracts.md): Specification of the onchain contracts that verify proof material, track game state, and release withdrawals for the Base proof system.
- [Design Goals](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-protocol/design-goals.md): Design philosophy and lineage of the Base Chain protocol specification.
- [B20 Token Standard](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/index.md): Native token standard for issuing programmable assets and stablecoins on Base, with roles, policies, supply controls, and ERC-20 compatibility.
- [Introduction](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/introduction.md): A short tour of tokens, roles, pause, and policies.
- [Token Types](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/concepts/token-types.md): Compare B20 Asset and Stablecoin variants, their creation parameters, and their capabilities.
- [Policies](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/concepts/policies.md): How B20 policies apply shared allowlists, blocklists, and composite checks to token operations.
- [Roles and Pause](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/concepts/roles-and-pause.md): How B20 roles authorize privileged operations and pause vectors control token features.
- [UI Multipliers](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/concepts/multipliers.md): How B20 Asset UI multipliers scale displayed balances without changing raw balances.
- [Interfaces](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/reference/interfaces.md): Canonical B20 Solidity interfaces, source links, and copy-paste imports.
- [Constants](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/reference/constants.md): B20 precompile addresses, role identifiers, policy scopes, and validation bounds.
- [Errors](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/reference/errors.md): Custom B20 errors, selectors, and the conditions that trigger them.
- [Events](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/reference/events.md): Events emitted by B20 token, factory, policy registry, and activation registry interfaces.
- [Changelog](https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/changelog.md): Per-hardfork, per-feature migration notes for the B20 token standard, newest first, including new methods, deprecations, and activation dates.
- [Transaction Ordering](https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/transaction-ordering.md): How transactions are ordered on Base, including block building with 200ms blocks and validity transactions.
- [Transaction Finality](https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/transaction-finality.md): Detailed information about transaction finality on Base.
- [Network Fees](https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/network-fees.md): How network fees on Base work, including L2 execution and L1 security fees, how the L1 fee is passed through, where fees go, how to estimate a transaction's total cost, and how to pay gas without ETH.
- [Throughput and Limits](https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/throughput-and-limits.md): Gas limits and throughput-related network parameters on Base.
- [Troubleshooting Transactions](https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/troubleshooting-transactions.md): Guide to diagnosing and resolving transaction issues on Base.
- [Validity Transactions](https://docs.base.org/specifications/build-transaction/validity-transactions.md): Submit signed transactions that Base considers when onchain conditions match.
- [Build a Validity Transaction](https://docs.base.org/specifications/build-transaction/build-a-validity-transaction.md): Sign and submit a validity transaction with Viem.
- [Validity Transaction RPC](https://docs.base.org/specifications/build-transaction/base_sendRawTransactionValidity.md): Submit a signed raw transaction with validity predicates.
- [Predicates and Safety](https://docs.base.org/specifications/build-transaction/predicates-and-safety.md): Use validity predicates safely, and understand expiry and replacement for validity transactions.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.base.org/specifications/build-transaction/troubleshooting.md): Diagnose validity transaction submission and inclusion issues.
- [Base Transactions](https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-transactions.md): EIP-8430 reference for Base: a new transaction type that allows for batching, sponsorship, token gas payments, and high throughput natively.
- [Base Builder Codes](https://docs.base.org/specifications/builder-codes/overview.md): Attribute onchain activity to your app, wallet or agent with Builder Codes.
- [Builder Codes for App Developers](https://docs.base.org/specifications/builder-codes/for-app-developers.md): Integrate Builder Codes into your app using Wagmi or Viem to attribute onchain activity.
- [Builder Codes for Wallet Developers](https://docs.base.org/specifications/builder-codes/for-wallet-developers.md): Implement the dataSuffix capability in your wallet to enable Builder Code attribution.
- [Builder Codes for Agent Developers](https://docs.base.org/specifications/builder-codes/for-agent-developers.md): Attribute your AI agent's onchain transactions to your identity on Base and make them measurable onchain.
- [Configuration](https://docs.base.org/specifications/reference/configuration.md): Reference for Base Chain configuration parameters across consensus, policy, admin, and sequencer categories.
- [Contract Addresses](https://docs.base.org/specifications/reference/base-contracts.md): A comprehensive list of contract addresses for Base Mainnet and Base Testnet, including links to their respective blockchain explorers.
- [Glossary](https://docs.base.org/specifications/reference/glossary.md): Glossary of terms and definitions used throughout the Base Chain protocol specification.
- [Run a Node](https://docs.base.org/specifications/node-operators/run-a-node.md): A tutorial that teaches how to set up and run a Base Node.
- [Node Performance](https://docs.base.org/specifications/node-operators/performance-tuning.md): Hardware specifications, storage requirements, client recommendations, and configuration settings for running a performant Base node.
- [Node Snapshots](https://docs.base.org/specifications/node-operators/snapshots.md): Download and restore Base node snapshots to significantly reduce initial sync time for nodes.
- [Node Troubleshooting](https://docs.base.org/specifications/node-operators/troubleshooting.md): Solutions to common issues when setting up and running a Base node, covering sync problems, networking, snapshots, and performance.
- [Security Council for Base](https://docs.base.org/specifications/security/security-council-for-base.md): This page outlines the purpose, goals, structure, and responsibilities of the Security Council for Base.
- [Reliability and Liveness](https://docs.base.org/specifications/security/reliability-and-liveness.md): Where to find Base network status, uptime, and incident history, third-party audits, bug bounties, censorship-resistance guarantees, proposal liveness, and the open-source sequencer components.
- [How to Avoid Getting Your App Flagged as Malicious](https://docs.base.org/specifications/security/avoid-malicious-flags.md): Best practices for keeping wallets and security tools from flagging your app as malicious, and how to report a false positive.
- [Reporting Vulnerabilities](https://docs.base.org/specifications/security/report-a-vulnerability.md): The Base bug bounty programs on HackerOne and Cantina, and how to report a security vulnerability.
- [SDKs & APIs](https://docs.base.org/sdks/overview.md): SDKs, APIs, and command-line tools for identity verification, local development, and direct Base chain access.
- [Foundry for Base](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-anvil.md): Build and test Base contracts with Foundry v1.8.4 or later, which runs Base's native precompiles, and v1.9.0 or later for the Denim upgrade. Set a Base hardfork to enable them locally.
- [Base RPC Overview](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/rpc-overview.md): Complete reference for all JSON-RPC methods available on Base nodes.
- [eth_blockNumber](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_blockNumber.md): Returns the number of the most recently mined block.
- [eth_call](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_call.md): Executes a message call without creating a transaction.
- [eth_chainId](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_chainId.md): Returns the chain ID of the current network.
- [eth_estimateGas](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_estimateGas.md): Estimates the gas required for a transaction.
- [eth_feeHistory](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_feeHistory.md): Returns historical base fees and priority fee percentiles for a range of blocks.
- [eth_gasPrice](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_gasPrice.md): Returns the current gas price in wei.
- [eth_getBalance](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getBalance.md): Returns the ETH balance of an account at a given block.
- [eth_getBlockByHash](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getBlockByHash.md): Returns block information by block hash.
- [eth_getBlockByNumber](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getBlockByNumber.md): Returns block information by number.
- [eth_getBlockReceipts](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getBlockReceipts.md): Returns all transaction receipts for a block.
- [eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash.md): Returns the number of transactions in a block by block hash.
- [eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber.md): Returns the number of transactions in a block by block number.
- [eth_getCode](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getCode.md): Returns the contract bytecode at an address.
- [eth_getLogs](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getLogs.md): Returns logs matching a filter.
- [eth_getStorageAt](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getStorageAt.md): Returns the value of a storage slot at an address.
- [eth_getTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex.md): Returns a transaction by block hash and index position.
- [eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex.md): Returns a transaction by block number and index position.
- [eth_getTransactionByHash](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getTransactionByHash.md): Returns a transaction by its hash.
- [eth_getTransactionCount](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getTransactionCount.md): Returns the number of transactions sent from an address (the nonce).
- [eth_getTransactionReceipt](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_getTransactionReceipt.md): Returns the receipt for a mined transaction. Receipts are only available after a transaction is included in a block.
- [eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas.md): Returns the suggested EIP-1559 priority fee (tip) per gas.
- [eth_sendRawTransaction](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_sendRawTransaction.md): Submits a pre-signed transaction to the network.
- [eth_simulateV1](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_simulateV1.md): Simulates one or more transaction bundles against canonical chain state, with optional state overrides, block overrides, and transfer tracing.
- [eth_subscribe](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_subscribe.md): Creates a real-time WebSocket subscription for new blocks, logs, and pending transactions.
- [eth_syncing](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_syncing.md): Returns the sync status of the node.
- [eth_unsubscribe](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/eth_unsubscribe.md): Cancels an active WebSocket subscription.
- [net_version](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/net_version.md): Returns the current network ID as a string.
- [web3_clientVersion](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/ethereum-json-rpc-api/web3_clientVersion.md): Returns the current client version string.
- [base_transactionStatus](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/base-api/base_transactionStatus.md): Checks whether a transaction is in the node mempool. Not available on the public Base endpoints.
- [debug_traceTransaction](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/debug-api/debug_traceTransaction.md): Returns the full EVM execution trace for a transaction. Requires a node with debug APIs enabled.
- [debug_traceBlockByHash](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/debug-api/debug_traceBlockByHash.md): Returns EVM execution traces for all transactions in a block by block hash.
- [debug_traceBlockByNumber](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/api-reference/debug-api/debug_traceBlockByNumber.md): Returns EVM execution traces for all transactions in a block by block number.
- [Tokenized Stocks API](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/overview.md): Read tokenized-stock records, supplies, metadata, prospectuses, and corporate actions on Base.
- [List Tokenized Stocks](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/api-reference/list-tokenized-stocks.md): Return the Coinbase-issued tokenized-stock records currently exposed through the API.
- [List Protocol Contract Addresses](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/api-reference/list-protocol-contract-addresses.md): Return the tokenized-stocks protocol contracts deployed on each supported chain.
- [List NAV Feed Addresses](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/api-reference/list-nav-feed-addresses.md): List configured Chainlink NAV price feeds for tokenized stocks on Base.
- [Get Token Total Supply](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/api-reference/get-token-total-supply.md): Return a tokenized stock's ERC-20 total supply, normalized by the token's decimals.
- [Get Token Metadata](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/api-reference/get-token-metadata.md): Return a tokenized stock's contractURI-compatible metadata document.
- [Get Token Icon](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/api-reference/get-token-icon.md): Redirect to a tokenized stock's icon using its ticker symbol.
- [Get Token Prospectus](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/api-reference/get-token-prospectus.md): Redirect to a tokenized stock's approved prospectus PDF.
- [List Cached Prospectuses](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/api-reference/list-cached-prospectuses.md): List cached approved prospectus documents by ticker, with ISINs when known.
- [Get Corporate Action](https://docs.base.org/sdks/tokenized-stocks/api-reference/get-corporate-action.md): Return a tokenized stock's announced or applied corporate action.
- [Base Earn API](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/overview.md): Earn and borrow on Base with the wallet you already use. Get unsigned transactions for Morpho and Upshift, then have the user's wallet sign and submit them.
- [Base Earn Concepts](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/concepts.md): Understand Morpho and Upshift vaults, withdrawal modes, atomic units, slippage bounds, and queued withdrawals in the Base Earn API.
- [Call the Base Earn API](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/call-the-api.md): Set up a backend helper in TypeScript, Python, or Go, or use cURL, to call the Base Earn API.
- [Execute Base Earn Calls in a Wallet](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/execute-calls.md): Verify and send the EIP-5792-style call batch returned by Base Earn API writes from a batch-capable wallet or an EOA with viem.
- [End-to-End Lend Examples](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/lend-example.md): Run a Morpho deposit and synchronous withdrawal, or an Upshift deposit, queued withdrawal, and claim, with the Base Earn API.
- [Morpho Borrow](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/morpho-borrow.md): Borrow a Morpho Blue market's loan asset against supported collateral on Base with the Base Earn API, including market selection, origination fees, and repayment.
- [List Vaults](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/api-reference/list-vaults.md): Return the Base Earn vault catalog with live onchain state, provider, withdrawal mode, token addresses, and decimals.
- [List Positions](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/api-reference/list-positions.md): Return an address's share balance and current asset value in every Base Earn vault.
- [Deposit](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/api-reference/deposit.md): Build the approve and deposit calls to put an asset into a Morpho or Upshift vault on Base.
- [Withdraw](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/api-reference/withdraw.md): Build the calls to withdraw an asset amount from a Morpho vault on Base in one step, with an explicit slippage bound.
- [Request Withdraw](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/api-reference/request-withdraw.md): Build the calls to queue Upshift vault shares for redemption and get an estimated claim date.
- [Get Redemption](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/api-reference/get-redemption.md): Check whether a queued Upshift redemption for an address, vault, and UTC date is claimable now.
- [Claim](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/api-reference/claim.md): Build the claim call that pays out a matured Upshift redemption to the user's address.
- [Borrow](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/api-reference/borrow.md): Build an unsigned, atomic transaction batch that borrows from a Morpho Blue market on Base, optionally adding collateral in the same batch.
- [Base Earn API Errors](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/errors.md): HTTP status codes, the error envelope, and retry guidance for Base Earn API errors.
- [Base Earn API FAQ](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-earn/faq.md): Answers to common questions about choosing a protocol, withdrawals, custody, accounts, API keys, liquidation risk, and Aave v4 in the Base Earn API.
- [Base Verify API](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-verify/overview.md): Use Base Verify APIs and contracts to prove verified account ownership, prevent duplicate participation, and enforce eligibility policies.
- [Verify Social Accounts](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-verify/verify-social-accounts.md): Use Base Verify to let users prove ownership of verified accounts (X, Coinbase, Instagram, TikTok) without sharing credentials, enabling Sybil-resistant airdrops, gated content, and identity-based rewards.
- [Verify Users Onchain](https://docs.base.org/sdks/base-verify/verify-users-onchain.md): Enforce Sybil resistance and policy gating inside any Base contract. Base Verify signs a short-lived verification your contract checks in the same transaction as a claim, deposit, or vote, so one real identity counts once and only wallets that meet your bar can participate.
- [Migrated and Deprecated Products](https://docs.base.org/sdks/migrated-products.md): Find where retired, moved, and renamed Base products went, including OnchainKit, MiniKit and mini apps, the Base Account SDK, Base MCP, Basenames, and Base App.
- [Upgrades](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/overview.md): Track Base network upgrades, activation dates, and the protocol changes included in each release.
- [Configuration Changelog](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/network-information/configuration-changelog.md): A log of configuration changes to the Base networks.
- [Everest](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/everest/overview.md): Everest introduces Base Transactions (EIP-8430), a new transaction type that allows for batching, sponsorship, token gas payments, and high throughput natively.
- [Denim](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/denim/overview.md): Denim introduces native blocks at a 200ms cadence, onchain millisecond time through BaseTime, millisecond-resolution RPC timestamps, and B20 transfer and policy improvements.
- [200ms Native Blocks](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/denim/200ms-blocks.md): Specification for Denim's canonical 200ms blocks, including BaseTime, derivation, validation, and RPC behavior.
- [Migrate From Flashblocks](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/denim/migrate-from-flashblocks.md): Migrate your Flashblocks integration to 200ms blocks.
- [B20: Reject the Token Itself as a Credit Recipient](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/specs/reference/b20/changelog/03-denim-b20-token-receiver.md): Denim reverts InvalidReceiver when a transfer, mint, or seize credits the B20 token's own address, so a mistyped recipient fails instead of locking funds.
- [B20: Transfer Executor Policy Enforcement](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/specs/reference/b20/changelog/03-denim-b20-transfer-executor-enforcement.md): Denim enforces TRANSFER_EXECUTOR_POLICY on msg.sender for every transfer path, closing the transfer and self-transferFrom bypasses.
- [PolicyRegistry: NOT / Invert Policies](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/specs/reference/b20/changelog/03-denim-policyregistry-not-policy.md): Denim reserves bit 63 of a policy ID as an invert flag, so isAuthorized returns the opposite of any policy's result without a second, mirrored policy.
- [Cobalt](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/cobalt/overview.md): Cobalt improves the B20 token standard, adds validity transactions, introduces dynamic node upgrades, and migrates TEE signer registration to onchain attestation verification.
- [Dynamic Upgrades](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/cobalt/dynamic-upgrades.md): An Ethereum smart contract stores upgrade timestamps for Base nodes, allowing forks to activate at the scheduled time with no client restart.
- [B20: ERC-8056 Conformant Multiplier](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/specs/reference/b20/changelog/02-cobalt-b20asset-multiplier.md): B20 Asset multiplier becomes ERC-8056 conformant at Cobalt, with a scheduled multiplier setter for corporate actions. Every Beryl selector stays dialable.
- [B20: Seize Functionality](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/specs/reference/b20/changelog/02-cobalt-b20-seize.md): The B20 seize surface at Cobalt and the deprecation of burnBlocked. Migration notes for teams integrated against the Beryl seize path.
- [PolicyRegistry: Composite Policies (UNION / INTERSECT)](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/specs/reference/b20/changelog/02-cobalt-policyregistry-composite-policy.md): Cobalt adds UNION and INTERSECT composite policies to PolicyRegistry so B20 integrations can combine simple authorization policies without flattening their member lists.
- [Validity Transactions](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/cobalt/validity-transactions.md): Validity transactions shipped with the Cobalt upgrade.
- [Beryl](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/overview.md): Beryl makes Base a first-class issuance platform with B20 tokens, more capital efficient with reduced withdrawal delays, and more scalable with Reth V2.
- [Reth V2](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/reth-v2.md): Ships Reth V2 as the reference execution client for Base nodes, delivering significant sync speed and throughput improvements.
- [Faster Withdrawals](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/reducing-canonical-withdrawal-delay.md): The single-proof dispute game finalization window is reduced from 7 days to 5 days. The dual-proof fast path (TEE + ZK) introduced in Azul remains at 1 day.
- [B20 Native Token Standard](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/beryl/b20.md): Learn how B20, Base's native token standard, serves stablecoin issuers, real-world asset (RWA) and equity issuers, and long-tail token creators.
- [Azul](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/azul/overview.md): Azul is Base's first independent network upgrade. It focuses on increasing security and decentralization, accelerating the path to 1 gigagas/s, and improving developer experience.
- [Node Upgrade Guide](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/azul/node-upgrade.md): Migrate your Base node to base-reth-node and base-consensus for Azul.
- [Execution Engine](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/azul/exec-engine.md): Execution engine changes in the Azul hardfork, including the EIP-7825 transaction gas limit cap and secp256r1 precompile cost updates.
- [Proof System](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/azul/proofs.md): Specification of the Azul multi-proof system, replacing the single output proposer with an AggregateVerifier contract for L2 checkpoint security.
- [Jovian](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/jovian/overview.md): Overview of the Jovian hardfork, introducing a configurable minimum base fee and a DA footprint gas scalar for improved fee market stability.
- [Jovian: Execution Engine](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/jovian/exec-engine.md): Execution engine changes in the Jovian upgrade, introducing a configurable minimum base fee via SystemConfig to reduce priority-fee auction durations.
- [Derivation](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/jovian/derivation.md): Derivation changes in the Jovian upgrade, specifying activation block rules and gas computation behavior at hardfork activation.
- [L1 Block Attributes](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/jovian/l1-attributes.md): L1 attributes transaction changes in the Jovian upgrade, extending calldata to include the DA footprint gas scalar.
- [Jovian: System Config](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/jovian/system-config.md): SystemConfig changes in the Jovian upgrade, adding a minimum base fee configuration variable for the EIP-1559 fee market.
- [Isthmus](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/isthmus/overview.md): Overview of the Isthmus hardfork, incorporating Ethereum Pectra EIPs and introducing the operator fee mechanism for sequencer revenue.
- [L2 Execution Engine](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/isthmus/exec-engine.md): Execution engine changes in the Isthmus upgrade, including L2ToL1MessagePasser storage root in block headers and operator fee collection.
- [Isthmus L2 Chain Derivation Changes](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/isthmus/derivation.md): Derivation changes in the Isthmus upgrade, specifying network upgrade automation transactions executed at hardfork activation.
- [L1 Block Attributes](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/isthmus/l1-attributes.md): L1 attributes transaction changes in the Isthmus upgrade, extending calldata to include operator fee scalar and constant parameters.
- [Predeploys](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/isthmus/predeploys.md): Predeploy changes in the Isthmus upgrade, including updates to L1Block and the new OperatorFeeVault contract.
- [Isthmus: System Config](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/isthmus/system-config.md): SystemConfig changes in the Isthmus upgrade, adding operatorFeeScalar and operatorFeeConstant configuration variables.
- [Holocene](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/holocene/overview.md): Overview of the Holocene hardfork, introducing dynamic EIP-1559 parameters configurable via SystemConfig and stricter block derivation rules.
- [L2 Execution Engine](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/holocene/exec-engine.md): Execution engine changes in the Holocene upgrade, enabling dynamic EIP-1559 parameters encoded in block headers and configured via SystemConfig.
- [Holocene L2 Chain Derivation Changes](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/holocene/derivation.md): Derivation changes in the Holocene upgrade, introducing stricter pipeline rules that simplify derivation and improve fault proof worst-case behavior.
- [System Config](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/holocene/system-config.md): SystemConfig changes in the Holocene upgrade, adding dynamic EIP-1559 parameter configuration via ConfigUpdate events.
- [Granite](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/granite/overview.md): Overview of the Granite hardfork, adding bn256Pairing precompile input size restrictions and CHANNEL_TIMEOUT parameter changes.
- [L2 Execution Engine](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/granite/exec-engine.md): Execution engine changes in the Granite upgrade, restricting bn256Pairing precompile input size to prevent unbounded gas consumption.
- [Granite L2 Chain Derivation Changes](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/granite/derivation.md): Derivation changes in the Granite upgrade, updating the CHANNEL_TIMEOUT protocol parameter.
- [Fjord](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/fjord/overview.md): Overview of the Fjord hardfork, introducing FastLZ-based L1 fee estimation, the RIP-7212 secp256r1 precompile, and brotli channel compression.
- [L2 Execution Engine](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/fjord/exec-engine.md): Execution engine changes in the Fjord upgrade, replacing the L1 cost fee estimator with a FastLZ-based compression model.
- [Fjord L2 Chain Derivation Changes](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/fjord/derivation.md): Derivation changes in the Fjord upgrade, updating protocol parameters for max sequencer drift, channel bank size, and adding brotli compression support.
- [Predeploys](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/fjord/predeploys.md): Predeploy changes in the Fjord upgrade, adding FastLZ fee computation constants to the GasPriceOracle contract.
- [Ecotone](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/ecotone/overview.md): Overview of the Ecotone hardfork, integrating Ethereum Dencun changes including EIP-4844 blob transactions and EIP-4788 beacon block roots.
- [Derivation](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/ecotone/derivation.md): Derivation changes in the Ecotone upgrade, extending the retrieval stage to support EIP-4844 blobs as an additional data availability source.
- [Ecotone L1 Attributes](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/ecotone/l1-attributes.md): L1 attributes transaction changes in the Ecotone upgrade, updating calldata format to support the new blob-based fee calculation model.
- [Delta](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/delta/overview.md): Overview of the Delta hardfork, introducing span batches to reduce L1 data costs by compressing multiple L2 blocks into single batcher transactions.
- [Span-Batches](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/delta/span-batches.md): Specification of span batches introduced in Delta, a new batch format that compresses sequences of L2 blocks for more efficient L1 data posting.
- [Canyon](https://docs.base.org/upgrades/canyon/overview.md): Overview of the Canyon hardfork, bringing Ethereum Shanghai EIPs (EIP-3651, EIP-3855, EIP-3860) to the Base execution layer.
